tasks.prompt: How does an incoming Request enter a Hono application, get matched to routes, and dispatch through one or multiple handlers?

answerPoints: app.fetch (an arrow property) passes the Request, env and execution context to the private #dispatch method
#dispatch matches method and path through this.router.match and creates a Context
exactly one matched handler is called directly (fast path), its result awaited and checked for a Response
several matched handlers/middleware run through compose(), and a non-finalized context afterwards is an error

tasks.prompt: How are Hono middleware handlers composed so next advances exactly once while errors and not-found responses are handled?

answerPoints: compose returns a function that runs an inner recursive dispatch(i) over the middleware array
an index check throws 'next() called multiple times' when next is called twice
when a handler throws and onError exists, context.error is set and onError's result becomes the response; without onError the error is rethrown
when no handler produced a response and the context is not finalized, onNotFound supplies the response

tasks.prompt: Why does the Hono class use SmartRouter wrapping RegExpRouter and TrieRouter by default, instead of using a single router, and what limitation does that design place on registering routes?

knowledge: context/decisions.md (### Default router is SmartRouter over RegExpRouter + TrieRouter)
answerPoints: RegExpRouter is the fastest (it compiles all routes into one regular expression) but rejects some path patterns by throwing UnsupportedPathError
SmartRouter tries its routers in order on the first match and keeps the first router that accepts every registered route, with TrieRouter as the general fallback
the choice is locked in lazily at the first match, so routes cannot be added after the first request has been matched (adding throws)

tasks.prompt: Inside a Hono built-in middleware, a shared auth helper returns c.text('Unauthorized', 401) when authentication fails. According to how this project is meant to be written, why is that the wrong approach, what should the helper do instead, and how does the alternative reach the client and the application's own error handling?

knowledge: context/conventions.md (## Patterns: signal HTTP errors by throwing HTTPException)
answerPoints: the helper should throw new HTTPException(401, ...) (optionally with a res or message) instead of returning an ad-hoc response
returning a response from deep inside a helper bypasses app.onError and the application's custom error handling
a thrown error is caught in compose/dispatch and routed to the error handler; the default errorHandler returns err.getResponse() for HTTPException-like errors and otherwise logs and returns a 500

tasks.prompt: Bug report: Hono's AWS Lambda adapter drops query parameters that are present but empty. Parameters whose value is undefined should still be omitted. Fix the adapter so present-but-empty values are preserved, add tests for it, and make sure the adapter's existing tests still pass.

Bug report: Hono's Lambda@Edge adapter decides whether a response body is binary with a different content-type check from the AWS Lambda adapter. Make the Lambda@Edge adapter's binary detection consistent with the AWS Lambda adapter's, add tests for it, and make sure the adapter's existing tests still pass.

tasks.prompt: Security bug report: Hono's JSX renderers trust the keys of an element's props. If an application spreads attacker-influenced data into an element, for example `<div {...userProps}>` where one key is `" onfocus="alert(1)` (or any key containing a quote, space, `<`, `>`, `/`, `=`, a backtick, a backslash or a control character), the key is written verbatim into the opening tag, so extra attributes or even new elements can be injected. The client-side DOM renderer (hono/jsx/dom) has the same defect in another shape: such a name makes the DOM throw, which aborts the render or a later update. Fix every place that emits attributes: (1) normal string rendering of elements, including elements inside `<svg>`, (2) the attribute helper in the jsx-runtime module that precompiled JSX uses, which must produce nothing for an invalid name whatever the value is (string, number, style object or promise) and must keep rendering valid ones exactly as before, (3) the DOM renderer, which must silently skip an invalid name both when first rendering and when an element is updated or its attribute removed, while any other error thrown by setAttribute or removeAttribute must still propagate. Ordinary names such as `class`, `data-foo`, `aria-label`, `viewBox`, `xml:lang`, `data.foo`, `data_foo` and non-ASCII letters stay valid; an empty name is invalid. Valid attributes next to an invalid one must still be rendered, in order. Add tests and make sure the existing JSX tests still pass.

code.symbol: jsxAttr (attribute helper of the automatic/precompiled runtime)

tasks.difficulty: Attributes are written in three independent places with three different mechanisms (string builder in JSXNode, the precompiled-JSX helper in jsx-runtime, and DOM setAttribute/removeAttribute with a different failure mode), so a fix in one leaves the others open; the DOM side must distinguish the invalid-name exception from other errors, and the string side must reject before the style/function/dangerouslySetInnerHTML branches. The symptom is a missing escape, not an error message, so nothing is greppable.

tasks.prompt: A POST route checks its input in a piece of middleware before the handler runs. Consider four requests to routes that validate (1) a JSON body sent with Content-Type application/json, (2) the same bytes sent with Content-Type text/plain, (3) a truncated, malformed JSON text sent with application/json, and (4) a url-encoded form body, sent to a route that validates the form. What does the user-supplied checking function receive in each case, and what does the client get back? And in case (1), once the middleware has run, how can the handler read the request body again through the request object (a request body stream can only be read once) and also fetch the validated result? Trace the pieces end to end.

code.symbol: validator (middleware: per-target value extraction, JSON/form parsing, 400s, addValidatedData)
HonoRequest.#cachedBody (per-representation body cache, rebuilds from another cached form)
compose (catches the thrown exception, calls onError)

answerPoints: The validator middleware chooses the value by target. For json it only parses when the Content-Type header matches a JSON media-type regex; it reads the body with c.req.json() and passes the parsed object to the checking function (case 1)

A missing or non-matching Content-Type (case 2, text/plain) is not an error: the body is not parsed and the checking function receives an empty object {}; the request is then not rejected by the middleware itself, whatever the checking function returns decides the outcome

Malformed JSON (case 3): c.req.json() rejects (JSON.parse of the cached text), the middleware catches it and throws HTTPException(400, 'Malformed JSON in request body'); compose catches the exception and the app's error handler turns it into the 400 response (the default handler uses getResponse(); an app.onError replaces that)

Form target (case 4): only multipart/form-data or application/x-www-form-urlencoded content types are parsed; the body is read once as an ArrayBuffer, converted to FormData with bufferToFormData and stored in bodyCache.formData; the FormData is flattened to an object where repeated keys (and keys ending in []) become arrays (so a=1&b=2&b=3 gives {a:'1', b:['2','3']}); a failure to parse throws HTTPException(400, 'Malformed FormData request.' + detail)

Re-reading and results: HonoRequest keeps a bodyCache with one promise per representation, and #cachedBody returns the cached promise or, if another representation is already cached, rebuilds a new Response from it (JSON is re-stringified, original Content-Type carried over except for FormData) so a second c.req.json()/text()/formData() works without touching the consumed stream. After the checking function returns a non-Response value, the middleware calls c.req.addValidatedData(target, value) (private #validatedData) and calls next; the handler reads it with c.req.valid(target). If the checking function returns a Response, that response is returned and next is not called

tasks.difficulty: The answer is split across the validator middleware (content-type gating, per-target parsing, the two 400 paths), the request class (a caching layer that is the reason a one-shot stream can be re-read, plus the validated-data store) and the exception/error-handling pipeline. The counter-intuitive result (wrong Content-Type is passed on as {} instead of rejected) is only visible in the middleware's switch.
